newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian film director De Santis dies aged 80.
newsitem.headline: Italian film director De Santis dies aged 80.

text.p: Director Giuseppe De Santis, one of the fathers of postwar Italian cinema, has died at the age of 80, hospital sources said on Saturday.
De Santis, perhaps best known for his 1949 film "Riso Amaro" (Bitter Rice), died in Rome's Sant'Eugenio hospital late on Friday after suffering a heart attack.

De Santis, who helped write Luchino Visconti's 1942 classic "Ossessione" (1942), was a champion of neorealism, which sought to highlight the miseries of Italian life following World War Two and the Fascist regime of dictator Benito Mussolini.
But many also considered De Santis, who had not directed a film for the past 20 years, to have heralded the end of neorealism.

"Bitter Rice", a melodramatic and sensual story set in the rice fields of the northern Po Valley, starred the sexy Silvana Mangano and was widely regarded as a commercial exploitation of the socially committed style.

Neorealism, whose greatest exponents were directors Roberto Rossellini and Vittorio De Sica, gradually died out in the 1950s as Italian cinema succumbed to an increasing trend for escapist entertainment.
De Santis's death came just a week after another great Italian director, Marco Ferreri, died of a heart attack in Paris at the age of 69.
"After (actor) Marcello Mastroianni and (director) Marco Ferreri, a third great artist of Italian cinema disappears," the organisers of the current Cannes Film Festival said in a statement.
"A poet of peasants and workers, he will remain as an unrivalled revolutionary moralist and filmmaker," they said.
